```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 12
    n_vehicles = 5
    Q = 57  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[26, 95], [16, 45], [89, 26], [25, 73], [87, 85], [71, 88], [95, 86], [58, 6], [58, 73], [78, 33], [84, 8], [22, 77]]
    demands = [21, 6, 10, 21, 13, 17, 7, 23, 15, 22, 24, 12]
    time_windows = [[0, 324], [65, 120], [47, 99], [41, 110], [55, 137], [61, 152], [47, 105], [65, 121], [67, 134], [23, 118], [55, 145], [57, 151], [50, 110]]
    service_times = [10, 6, 15, 11, 13, 14, 15, 8, 14, 5, 9, 12]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Memo: Vehicle Routing and Scheduling for Today’s Deliveries

Purpose and Context
We will execute a day-of-delivery plan from our central depot using a fleet of identical vehicles. The service area consists of a set of geographically dispersed customers, each identified by map coordinates and each with an agreed delivery window. The workday is anchored at time 0, which is when all dispatched vehicles leave the depot. The planning horizon ends at the depot’s closing time as defined in the data set (see Annex).

Routing and Scheduling Challenge
- Each assigned vehicle will complete a single trip: depart the depot at time 0, visit an ordered sequence of customers, and return to the depot before the depot closes. No vehicle will run multiple tours.
- Every customer must be visited exactly once. Split deliveries are not allowed.
- Travel time between any two locations is assumed to equal the straight-line distance between their coordinates, with speed set to 1, so time and distance share the same units.
- Routes should be geographically sensible and time-feasible, balancing customer commitments with vehicle availability and deployment cost.

Service Commitments and Operating Rules
- Time windows: The start of service at each customer must fall within the customer’s delivery window. If a vehicle arrives before the window opens, it must wait until the window start before beginning service. Arrivals after the window closes are not permitted.
- Service times: Each stop includes a specified unloading/service time. Departure from a customer occurs at the later of the arrival time or the window opening, plus the service time.
- Capacity: All vehicles have the same carrying capacity. The total customer demand assigned to any one route must not exceed this capacity at any point in the trip.
- Depot timing: All vehicles depart at time 0 and must return to the depot before the depot’s closing time. Returns after closing are not permitted.

Cost Considerations
- Using a vehicle incurs a fixed deployment cost in addition to the distance-based travel cost of the route.
- Because each vehicle carries a fixed cost, it may be cost-effective to serve all customers with fewer vehicles if feasible. However, any such consolidation must still meet time windows, service durations, and capacity constraints.
- The goal is to minimize total cost, defined as the sum of all route distances plus the fixed cost for each vehicle used, while meeting all operational rules.

Outcome Sought
We need a set of feasible vehicle routes that:
- Start at the depot at time 0 and return before the depot closes,
- Visit every customer exactly once,
- Begin service within each customer’s time window (waiting is allowed if early),
- Observe service times at each stop,
- Respect vehicle capacity limits, and
- Minimize total travel distance and vehicle deployment costs.
